entityChanges.reason: EC-14 (G-14). Vital statistics grew from mortality-table analysis (Graunt 1662, Halley 1693) and civil registration (Farr), not from calculus. nodes.name: Tin bronze
nodes.prereqRationale: ore_prospecting (D11 new id, A3 trunk) replaces copper_smelting, which it requires and therefore still guarantees: tin bronze needs the smelting of copper AND the recognition of cassiterite (stream-tin placers and lode outcrops) as tin ore - tin sources were the Bronze Age bottleneck, and the D11 identification contract names ore_prospecting as the exposed tin-ore identification. The explicit 'copper_smelting AND ore_prospecting' form D02 had offered would be a redundant conjunct (copper_smelting is implied) that raises prereq_complexity without adding knowledge. Chronology: tin_bronze's earliest marked year (~4,650 BCE) lies before 3000 BCE, so the test does not check it; ore_prospecting (~5,000 BCE) is earlier in any case.

capability.currentEffect: MEASURED (unlock audit class B): makes recipe.bronze_casting eligible - goods.json bronze-casting: 8 copper-ore + 1 tin-ore + 2 timber -> 1 bronze per execution, 0.4 person-years, also requires artisan_share > 0.05 - and satisfies a3_bronze. copper-ore (spread 0.8) and tin-ore (spread 0.9) are per-settlement deposits on the elevation channel, extracted ungated from turn 1. Bronze is the only input metal of the baseline toolmaking recipe (1 bronze + 1 timber -> 2 tools), so this node is the knowledge gate of all domestic tool production: the farm tool factor (up to +30 %, toolYieldBonusMax 0.3), the workshop project (10 tools) and highway roads (1 tool per km), unless bronze or tools arrive by trade. The node's factors match its peers, but its only prerequisite was charcoal, so bloomery smelting - reducing ore with charcoal in a furnace at roughly 1,100-1,300 C - was reachable with no furnace knowledge at all; that missing edge, not the scoring, made its closure (10 nodes / 14,320 RP) cheaper than the A3 CORE fact (9 / 15,250). kiln_updraft (an enclosed firing chamber, controlled atmosphere, 'the thermal precondition for smelting') is the knowledge every centre needed, including the sub-Saharan clay shaft furnaces (INFERENCE: the tree's kiln node stands for building an enclosed high-temperature chamber, which a smelting furnace is). Copper smelting stays an accelerator, not a requirement: the node's own Eureka (when: copper_smelting) says so ('Not a prerequisite: African iron may be independent'); making it a prerequisite would make that Eureka implied, which the loader refuses (Eurekas are append-only), and would deny the debated independent-invention route. Bellows were not used: their emerged (~1,500 BCE) post-dates iron (~1,800 BCE) and the chronology test would fail (D06 request).

nodes.rationale: Causal prerequisite and anchor fix. Predictive geometric models need mean motions, and the Greeks took those from Babylonian calendrical astronomy. The 19-year luni-solar cycle (Babylon from ~499 BCE; Meton 432 BCE) underlies the Callippic and Hipparchic year and month lengths. The edge therefore runs through calendar_lunisolar, which still requires astronomy_records. The anchor adds Hipparchus, whose solar and lunar models came three centuries before the Almagest.

nodes.rationale: Research-stage finding (culturally narrow). Because algebra required geometry_axiomatic, the stage atom '(geometry_axiomatic OR algebra)' offered no real alternative: every path to the stage held Greek axiomatic geometry. Al-Khwarizmi's geometric demonstrations drew on Euclid, but algebra itself did not need them. Brahmagupta (628 CE) gave rules for zero, negatives and the quadratic without Euclidean proof. The Chinese fangcheng (Nine Chapters) and Song–Yuan polynomial algebra (1247–1303 CE) grew from counting-rod computation. Algebra's causal requirements are a positional calculating system and the area-based problem tradition of practical geometry. The Indian/Islamic route (hindu_arabic) and the Chinese route (counting_rods) both cost more than the Greek route to the stage, so the stage is broadened without being made cheaper.

nodes.rationale: The node bundled Otto's 1876 stationary four-stroke gas engine with the Daimler-Maybach and Benz high-speed petrol engines of 1883-86 (its own text: 'Otto 1876 four-stroke; Daimler/Benz 1885 vehicle'). These are distinct knowledge with distinct consumers: the stationary gas engine is the principle (internal combustion, the compression cycle) and the root of Diesel's engine; the high-speed engine needed refined liquid fuel and light, fast construction, and is what aircraft, cars, tanks and tractors use. The key stays with the high-speed engine, which keeps every current consumer and the A9 CORE fact a9_combustion, so no other lane must re-point (D01, D08, D09 already require internal_combustion for vehicles). The founding part becomes gas_engine, which takes the engine-architecture, combustion-chemistry and machining prerequisites. Liquid fuel is now explicit: Daimler's and Benz's engines ran on light petroleum spirit (ligroin, bought at a pharmacy on Bertha Benz's 1888 drive - RESEARCHED).

The nucleus (1911) and isotopes (1913) are precursors folded into this node; its dated anchor is the neutron (1932), so the chronology rule holds with quantum_mechanics (1925).
